hypothesis: In tornado.escape, the xhtml_escape/url_escape family of functions mishandles non-ASCII or special characters under the C locale, producing incorrect escaping output.
trigger: Call tornado.escape.xhtml_escape on a string containing non-ASCII characters and special HTML characters, and tornado.escape.url_escape on a string with non-ASCII characters, under LC_ALL=C.
potential_failure: The escaping functions may raise UnicodeEncodeError or produce incorrectly escaped output when handling non-ASCII characters under the C locale.

oracle.expected_behavior: xhtml_escape should correctly escape HTML special characters and preserve non-ASCII characters; url_escape should percent-encode non-ASCII characters correctly.
oracle.target_evidence: tornado/escape.py contains xhtml_escape and url_escape functions that are documented to handle unicode strings. The module uses to_unicode and utf8 conversions.
oracle.historical_evidence: cookiecutter:1 showed a bug where file reading without explicit encoding caused wrong decoding on Windows; PySnooper:3 showed a variable name bug. Neither directly transfers, but both suggest encoding-related bugs are common.
